question: Rakesh has to fill water in a cylindrical container of height 10 cm and radius 10 cm with a hemispherical bowl of radius 5 cm. How many times does he have to pour water into the cylindrical container with the hemispherical bowl to fill the tank completely with water?
solution:
**Given:**

Height of cylindrical container: 10 cm

Radius of cylindrical container: 10 cm

Radius of hemispherical bowl: 5 cm

**Concept:**

Volume of water required to fill the cylindrical container will be equal to the volume of water poured using the hemispherical bowl multiple times.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of cylindrical container = πr²h = π(10 cm)²(10 cm) = 1000π cm³

⇒ Volume of hemispherical bowl = 2/3πr³ = 2/3π(5 cm)³ = 250π/3 cm3

⇒ Number of times required to pour = Volume of cylinder/Volume of each pour = 1000π cm³/(250π/3 cm³) = 12

**Therefore, Rakesh has to pour water into the cylindrical container with the hemispherical bowl 12 times to fill the tank completely with water.**
